solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Barking canine hassling boxer’s vulnerability (9, two words)

indicators.note: barking means mad, so the letters that follow go wild and rearrange themselves

blocks.note: C stands for a canine tooth in the dental formula

explanation.surface: A mad dog harassing a boxer exposes his weak spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canine' looks like the barking dog, but it is reduced to its dental-chart symbol C.
explanation.definitionFit: A fighter who is easily knocked out is said to have a glass chin, the classic weakness of a boxer.

clue.text: Ghost once seen in cellar vault

indicators.note: the answer can be seen sitting inside the run of letters across the next two words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A spectre glimpsed long ago down in a wine cellar's vault.
explanation.definitionFit: In Latin and in obsolete English usage a larva was a ghost or spectre, hence the word 'once' in the definition.

clue.text: Tabloids regularly featuring it? (5, two words)

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so take every second letter of the words that follow

blocks.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters
the alternation carries on into this word

explanation.surface: A wry question about what popular newspapers keep putting on their pages.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Tabloids' and 'it' as one string and every second letter spells A-LIST; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The A-list is the top tier of celebrities, exactly the people gossip papers write about week after week.

clue.text: Family member lives in outskirts of St Louis

indicators.note: one piece goes in, between the two outer letters supplied by the rest

blocks.note: to live is to exist, i.e. to be: 'is'
the outside letters of St Louis

explanation.surface: A relative has settled on the edge of the American city of St Louis.
explanation.definitionFit: Siss is a dialect or familiar form of sister, a female sibling and so a relation in the family.

clue.text: Grass on school truant

blocks.note: to play the wag is to play truant, so a wag is a truant

explanation.surface: Someone informs on a pupil skipping school.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' looks like a verb meaning inform; it is the noun for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Schwag is slang for low-grade marijuana, and grass is the everyday slang term for the same drug.

clue.text: Resistance about amount wasted on urban area

indicators.note: something wasted is ruined and broken up, so these letters are scrambled

blocks.note: C is circa, Latin for about
taken as written, to be rearranged
a city is a large urban area

explanation.surface: Opposition to a sum of money squandered on developing a town.
explanation.definitionFit: Contumacity is stubborn disobedience or defiance of authority, a form of obstinate opposition.

clue.text: Traveller’s inn, the very thing to stall horse

indicators.note: to stall an animal is to shut it inside an enclosure, so one piece encloses the other

blocks.note: 'that's it' means that's the very thing

explanation.surface: At a roadside inn, the perfect spot to stable your horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An imaret is a Turkish hospice offering lodging to pilgrims and travellers on their journey.

clue.text: Chambers English work affected person

blocks.note: to work something is to use it

explanation.surface: Reads like the Chambers English dictionary at work on someone pretentious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chambers' looks like the dictionary publisher but is the plural of chamber pot; a po is a chamber pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A poseuse is a woman who strikes attitudes to impress others, i.e. someone with affected manners.

clue.text: Solvent removing all traces of faeces in sewage outflow

indicators.note: every letter standing for the named word is to be taken out, not just one

blocks.note: the first letter, a trace of the word

explanation.surface: A cleaning fluid that removes every bit of muck from sewage discharge.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Fs go, which is why the clue says all traces.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry an eluent is the liquid solvent used to wash substances through a chromatography column.

clue.text: Companies dealt with peasant farmer

indicators.note: something dealt with has been handled and processed, so its letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Firms have done business with a smallholder.
explanation.definitionFit: Campesino is the Spanish and Latin American word for a rural labourer or small farmer working the land.

clue.text: Spotted animal can briefly turn docile after scratching flanks

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter
scratching the flanks strikes out the letters on both sides of the word
to turn the word round is to read it from the other end

explanation.surface: A wild beast with spots may calm down once you stop it clawing at its sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A calico is a cat with a blotched coat of white, black and orange, so a spotted or patched animal.

clue.text: Self-important official to criticise judge plus a suspect

blocks.note: to pan a show is to criticise it

explanation.surface: A pompous bureaucrat sets out to attack a judge and a dubious suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: Panjandarum is a variant of panjandrum, a mock title for a pompous person who acts as if he were very powerful.

clue.text: Resources low indeed!

blocks.note: la is an old exclamation of emphasis or surprise

explanation.surface: An exclamation that funds are running short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' looks like an adjective about the resources; it is the cow's noise.
explanation.definitionFit: Moola is slang for money, and money is one's financial resources or means.

clue.text: Avatar perhaps ranks No 1 in Hollywood I suspect

indicators.note: the number one letter of the word, that is its first, is wanted
as an adjective suspect means dodgy and not to be trusted as it stands, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Reads like a guess that the film Avatar tops the Hollywood rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: Avatar suggests the James Cameron film; here it is the Hindu sense of a god in earthly form.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hinduism Krishna is the eighth incarnation of the god Vishnu, and an incarnation is an avatar; 'perhaps' flags an example.

clue.text: Public notices hint of hesitation here

explanation.surface: Announcements posted here, with a slight pause.
explanation.definitionFit: Adsum is Latin for 'I am present', the reply at a roll call, just as a pupil answers 'here'.

clue.text: Caring and feeding of cattle is leaving 20 suffering

indicators.note: the named letters leave, taken away from the longer word
something suffering is in a bad way and knocked out of shape, so its letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: Livestock husbandry is giving up on puzzle-setters in distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Agistment is the taking in of other people's livestock to graze on one's land for payment, i.e. pasturing them.

clue.text: Mock almost completed — with Q 17 what’s 16, 4×4?

indicators.note: only almost completed means the word stops one letter short of its end

blocks.note: Q is the 17th letter of the alphabet; the 16th comes just before it

explanation.surface: Looks like a cryptic maths question, ending with four times four.
explanation.walkthrough: The numbers are alphabet positions: if Q is 17, letter 16 is P. And 4×4 is not sixteen but a four-wheel-drive vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A Jeep is the original four-wheel-drive off-road vehicle, and a 4×4 is the general name for such cars.

clue.text: What’s essential to indulge with grand afternoon meal?

definitions.text: What’s essential to indulge with grand afternoon meal?

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very core, so take its middle letter

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
a. is a dictionary abbreviation for afternoon
tea is a light meal in the late afternoon in Britain
the fourth of its seven letters

explanation.surface: Asks what treat you need for a grand indulgent afternoon tea.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: a cake is the essential indulgence at a posh afternoon tea, a British light meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich layered cream cake, the centrepiece treat on a lavish tea table.

clue.text: Meagre sputtering summer period?

indicators.note: a sputtering speaker gets out a fragment of the word before managing it whole, so only part comes first

blocks.note: a stammered start on the month: just its outer letters

explanation.surface: A thin, spluttering start to summer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jejune means thin, scanty and unsatisfying, so lacking substance in the way a meagre portion does.

clue.text: Cryptic games isn’t it for such?

definitions.text: Cryptic games isn’t it for such?

indicators.note: cryptic means coded and obscure, so the letters that follow are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Asks whether cryptic puzzles are just the thing for people who love riddles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: cryptic games are indeed for these people.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatists are makers or solvers of riddles and puzzles, and crossword setters often use the word of themselves.

clue.text: Returning on court with rubber bat

indicators.note: returning means coming back the other way, so the first small word is read backwards

blocks.note: ule is a Central American rubber tree

explanation.surface: A player comes back on court holding a rubber-faced bat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bat' looks like the table-tennis bat of the surface; it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The noctule is a large reddish-brown European bat, so the answer is a specific kind of the flying mammal.

clue.text: Icy terrain? Throw in grit then slippery character’s receding

indicators.note: one word is put inside another
something receding goes backwards, so the last piece is written back to front

explanation.surface: Advice for an icy road: spread grit, as anyone slippery backs away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Icy terrain' suggests a frozen road needing grit; it means landscape shaped by ice sheets.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoss and lee describes glaciated topography where rocks have a gentle smoothed side facing the ice flow and a steep plucked side away.

clue.text: Wick’s tangled tight in tip of taper

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, applied to each of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: A candle wick has got snarled tightly at the end of the taper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wick' is not the candle part but the town of Wick in northern Scotland, so 'Wick's' signals a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tautit is Scots for matted or tangled, used of hair or wool, so it is how a Scot says tangled.

clue.text: Nap from a tipster is failing, not getting trip unfortunately

indicators.note: something failing is falling apart, so these letters break up and re-form
the letters of the named word are not received, so they are removed
unfortunately signals things gone awry, so the removed letters may come out in any order

blocks.note: taken as written, its letters scattered within the fodder

explanation.surface: A doze that comes from a racing tipster losing and missing out on a holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is an afternoon rest or short sleep, customary in hot countries, which is a nap.

clue.text: Tope and traipse around to a degree …

indicators.note: turning around faces the word the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: to gad about is to traipse around
the article taken as written; 'to' is a link

explanation.surface: Drinking hard and wandering about, up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tope' looks like the verb to drink heavily; it is the noun for a Buddhist shrine.
explanation.definitionFit: A dagaba, or dagoba, is a Buddhist dome-shaped relic shrine, and tope is another name for such a stupa.

clue.text: Strategy switching first two pieces in Xs and Os?

indicators.note: only the first two pieces of the three-part name are kept, the last dropped
switching swaps the order, so the two pieces change places

blocks.note: the pencil game of noughts and crosses

explanation.surface: A game plan for noughts and crosses: swap your first two moves.
explanation.walkthrough: Tic-tac-toe is the American name for noughts and crosses; its first two syllables trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A tactic is a planned manoeuvre for achieving an end, which is a close synonym of a strategy.

clue.text: Me? I’d unwind with an occasional Scotch

indicators.note: to unwind is to loosen and come apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone relaxing with a whisky now and then.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scotch' looks like the whisky but labels the answer as a Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: Daimen is a Scots adjective meaning rare or occasional, as in Burns's 'a daimen icker in a thrave'.

clue.text: … I idly walk about like an aborigine

definitions.note: adjectival phrase; the answer is used as an adjective

indicators.note: turning about faces the whole string the other way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: to roam is to wander aimlessly

explanation.surface: Someone describes wandering lazily about like a native of the land.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links back to the previous clue but adds nothing to this one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Maori are the indigenous Polynesian people of New Zealand, so Maori describes an aboriginal inhabitant there.

clue.text: Cream cake’s last thing that’s good for slimmers

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is the one taken

blocks.note: lite food has reduced fat or calories

explanation.surface: A cream cake as the final treat a dieter should allow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cream' looks like the topping on the cake; it is the noun for the best of a group.
explanation.definitionFit: The elite are the best or choicest members of a group, the cream of the crop.

clue.text: International corporation backing traditional medicine in SA

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the joined pieces are read from right to left

blocks.note: corporation is old slang for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A global company supporting folk remedies in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like the company; in old slang it means a paunch.
explanation.definitionFit: Muti is the South African term for traditional herbal or magical medicine, as used by a sangoma or healer.

clue.text: Vacuum clearing house throughout

indicators.note: clearing something out removes it, so those letters are taken away

blocks.note: to hoover is to vacuum, from the brand name

explanation.surface: Vacuuming while cleaning the entire house.
explanation.definitionFit: Over can mean through the whole extent of something, as in 'all over the world', i.e. throughout.

clue.text: Holiday company boarding European with small cases

indicators.note: a boarder lodges inside someone else's house, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: TUI is a large European travel firm

explanation.surface: A tour operator puts a European passenger on board with only small luggage.
explanation.definitionFit: Étuis are small ornamental cases for needles, cosmetics or other little articles.

clue.text: Turning right nearly miss glimpse of Santa’s sleigh

indicators.note: turning round means facing the other way, so the abbreviation is read backwards
nearly means not quite all, so the last letter is lost
a glimpse shows only the very first bit, so take the initial letter

blocks.note: to miss something is to avoid it

explanation.surface: Swerving right, narrowly missing a glimpse of Father Christmas's sleigh.
explanation.definitionFit: A travois is a Native American sledge of two poles dragged by a horse or dog, a sleigh-like carrier.

clue.text: River dweller’s fate after returning home

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for home is read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone living by a river meets their destiny after coming home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the fate word behind the reversed home word.
explanation.definitionFit: A Nilot is a member of one of the peoples of the Upper Nile valley, so literally a dweller by that river.

clue.text: Such fruitfulness takes pressure off teens?

definitions.text: Such fruitfulness takes pressure off teens?

indicators.note: takes ... off means removes, so the letter is subtracted from the word

blocks.note: puberty is the stage of the teenage years

explanation.surface: Asks whether a fertile spell might ease the strain on adolescents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teens' stands for the life stage, not the people.
explanation.definitionFit: Uberty is an archaic word for fertility, abundance and plenteous productiveness.

clue.text: Mature woman removing half of wine jugs

indicators.note: half the word is taken away, leaving only its first part

explanation.surface: An older woman pouring away half her white wine from the jugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jugs' looks like wine jugs; it is slang for breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Mammaries are the milk glands, i.e. breasts, and jugs is crude slang for a woman's breasts.
